message.content: The sculpture that most people think of when they picture the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** (originally conceived in 1880–1881, first cast in 1902). Its dramatic pose, psychological depth, and the fact that it has been reproduced in countless editions made it the iconic image of modern sculpture—and it remains one of the most recognizable works from that era.
